newsitem.title: USA: Ashland Coal Q1 costs at record low.
newsitem.headline: Ashland Coal Q1 costs at record low.

text.p: Ashland Coal Inc said Thursday it had a strong first quarter with record sales and production achieved at record low cost of sales.
But it warned the impact of cost cuts will be offset in future quarters.
The company earned $12.3 million, or $0.65 per share on a fully diluted basis, in the first quarter. A year earlier, it had net income of $1.5 million, or $0.07 per share.
Revenues for the first quarter were $166.6 million in 1997 and $143.3 million in 1996. Coal sales were 6.4 million tons this year, and 5.2 million tons in the same period last year.

Results for the first quarter reflected higher production and lower costs as a result of operational changes implemented during 1996, Ashland Coal said. The relocation of the large dragline from the Hobet 07 complex to the Dal-Tex complex was the primary contributor to the improved results.

In the latest quarter, the company said, it recorded a charge related to an idled processing facility of about $2.1 million, which was partially offset by a change in the estimate of the company's liability for postmining reclamation and mine closure of about $1.4 million.

It noted results for the first quarter of 1996 were hurt by severe winter weather and a $3.8 million restructuring charge, offset in part by a payment received upon an agreed reduction of 1996 deliveries under a sales contract.

"The strong earnings in the first quarter, in which we set sales and production records and achieved record low cost of sales, were gratifying," said chief executive William C. Payne. "Over the remainder of the year we expect cost improvements at the Hobet 21 complex as the benefits of the dragline move across Mud River are fully realized as well as when the overland conveyor is completed in the third quarter.
"However, these improvements are expected to be offset by cost increases elsewhere," he said.
